Q-PART-2.notes:
I think movement must be based on sub-regions, otherwise we'll have to deal with funny issues like a surrounded army slipping through to friendly territory. Lets try this ruleset:
1. Armies in contested territory by default attack for that territory. they can only attack or withdraw. they cannot entrench, or re-moraleize, or anything else.
2. Withdrawing can only happen to an adjacent territory, and armies can only pass through friendly sub-territories to get there. This prevents that silly case from earlier
3. You can only collect income/resources if you control the entire territory. You can only recruit/train if the territory is uncontested. Only militia will come to arms from within a contested territory if an order to call them was submitted when the territory became contested. Any other army will remain stuck. 

These represent the chaos a region is under when contested, while also keeping the game's scope at grand strategy. I feel going full in on sub-territories makes it a little too tactical.

Q-PART-3.notes: I think I want automatic. Bascially defenders should strongly keep territories around the territory capital and weakly neighboring friendly territories, depending on how bad they lost. Setting up for a siege the defender should get a +1 die role for city barricades. For 3/N-way attack resolution, the defender is who ever controls the Capital, or had control of the territory last.

Q-PROC-2.notes:
One important note about the revs, and this is likely important to include in the memory, but the revs were essentially attempts. rev 1: implement all of milestone 2; then I play tested recorded feedback and that fed into rev 2; where we tried to fix everything, I play tested, recorded feedback, etc. So as the revs go on, ideally they are lighter and lighter passes. This also means we should be able to keep the coordinator and worker agent pattern; have more parallel worker agents(doing more work per rev); and we should using the agentic loop pattern for each sub agent, so they are able to do more independently. We should also give workers token limits/checkpoints; so they can check in with a supervisor agent to ensure they're not stuck in a infinite loop/are deadlocked burning tokens.

Again, the goal for each rev is that Production Ready(put it in the hands of paying customers; demo with Director) AND coding quality bar.

Q-RAIL-2.notes:
A unit can:
1. move 1 territory (if it doesn't have a truck)
2. move 1 territory and take rail to friendly territory
3. take rail to friendly territory and then move 1 territory penalty free

Q-RAIL-3.notes: Build, Upgrade, Repair, this is all done on a sub-territory basis. A line uses the lowest level rail that the unit passes to get to its destination. This means that the unit needs to path on the rail.

Q-RAIL-4.notes: If its a clean handover, nothing. If the region becomes contested, the attacker held sub-territories rail gets downgraded.

Q-RAIL-5.notes:
In our north star, we may want to treat rail conversion/gauge switching as a necesarry step in invading in a WW1/2 scenario.

I want to treat rail as a sub-territory capability, with effects that live in the game's scenario data file. This should be a type of movement modifier. This is because I don't want it to limit napoleon or 7yrs war, which didn't have rail.

Similarly, armies should be able to recruit trucks as unit that give the army movement bonus. I am fixing the terminology now: An army is specifically a group of units that originate from the same territory and get the same orders. A unit is just a piece of that. So a truck, or artillery, or etc. give bonuses to the army that is apart of for that turn. 

Also, not related to rail gauge, but we need to iterate on the rail UX screen shots, specifically how they show up on the grand map. The lines should be thinner, and since they're a property of a sub-territory, it should be obvious how the rails are tied there. Lets use bezier curves for the rail's shape. Adjacent sub-territories each with rail are automatically connected.

Rail is a sub-territory movement bonus, similar to moving along rivers. Where as mountainous regions or swampy give movement penalties. An army can always move atleast 1 territory, where trucks would give a plus 1 to that, but mountains or swamp would subtract 1.

Q-RECR-2.notes:
Each territory should have a capital sub-territory. Recruitement can happen there. Recruitment requires: Money, Manpower, and certain buildings to be present. The "tagged can-recruit" in the scenario data is not needed; what's needed is the more provincal territory capitals should be missing the necesarry buildings to train proper regiments (e.g. only militia). A barracks enables infantry, a barracks and factory enable artillery, a factory and supply depot enable trucks, etc. 

A player should be able to see all of the unit types, but some unit types should be greyed out and a hover will show what buildings or resources are missing.
